# Stories to do

Put each story here as its own plain-text file (.txt or .md), in plain English, with its tracker id if it
has one: "INJ-592 A visitor can send the contact form". Then ask the AI to do the stories:
stories/AI-INSTRUCTIONS.md tells it how. A story it implements moves to stories/done/. This README is
not a story.

## A story the AI can implement

- **An outcome**, something a visitor sees at the end: "Then the cart shows 2 items". A list of
  acceptance criteria is welcome: each criterion becomes a test of its own, numbered by its place in
  your list (INJ-592-1, INJ-592-2, ...), so keep the list in the order you mean and add to its end.
- **The steps before it**, one per line, each a link, button or field in the site's own words: "Start
  on the home page. Click Contact Us in the footer." Steps and conditions ("two books may share a
  price") are not outcomes.
- **An outcome the steps make true**: a message already on the page before the click proves nothing.
  Name what changes. What a page shows as it opens is fine to check, a heading's words too. Write
  **page title** for the words in the browser tab and **heading** for the big words on the page: a
  plain "title" could be either, and comes back to you with both. That a page opens at all is checked
  already, by every test.
- **The id as the file name writes it**, once.

## A story sent back to you

A story the AI can't turn into a test that checks what it says stays here, with its reasons appended
under a `---- PUSHBACK` line. Under that, when a rewrite would make it testable, the AI proposes one, under
a `---- PROPOSED REWRITE` line. **Once a story is pushed back, its text above the `---- PUSHBACK` line is
the record of what was asked: never edit it.** Do one of these, then ask for the stories again:

- **Accept the rewrite:** delete everything above the `---- PROPOSED REWRITE` line, that line too; or
  add `Answer: yes` on a line under the rewrite. The rewrite is now the story.
- **Correct the rewrite:** edit it, then delete everything above it, as above.
- **Answer:** under each line of the push-back's Needed list (or a `Needs from you:` line) that you can
  answer, add one line starting `Answer:` in your own words: "Answer: yes, a test may send this form";
  "Answer: the second one"; "Answer: saved-pages/<folder>/after-send.html". Change nothing else. The AI
  reads your answers on its next pass and writes or implements the story from them.
- **Leave it:** if you cannot answer yet, leave the file exactly as it is: it is the record of what is
  needed, and the AI lists it as waiting on you.

**Never write the story yourself in this file.** A story of your own drops what the push-back asked for
or asks something else, and comes back for the same reason. A different story is a new file with a new
id. A `Needs from you:` line is never deleted: answer it on the line under it, or the story waits.

**What only you can give.** A permission (in your words, on an `Answer:` line). A choice between the
things the push-back names. A page the crawl never saw: you save it yourself, as a visitor sees it
after the steps (in a browser, open the page, press F12, right-click the `<html>` line, Copy, Copy
outerHTML, and paste it into a new .html file in the saved-pages/ folder the push-back names). Nobody
else can: the AI has no browser and does not know the state you mean.

## A story partly done

A story with a list of acceptance criteria gets a test for each the AI can check, and moves to
stories/done/ with an IMPLEMENTED note. Its `Not implemented:` lines are the criteria it could not
check, each with its number and what it needs. To get one done, leave the file in stories/done/ and add
a line starting `Answer:` under it, as for a story sent back; the AI's next pass writes its test, with
its own number, and adds a new note. The tests it already has stay as they are.

Until you do one of these, the AI leaves the story alone and lists it as waiting on you. A rewrite never
changes what the business asked for: where the only testable story is a different one, the AI says so
instead of proposing it.
